evidence: Receiving DO2 collapse at t=46.2h: 12.25 -> 3.69 mg/L (receiving_observations)
DO2 at/below 2.0 mg/L minimum: 1.67 (51.8h), 1.73 (52.0h), 1.96-2.4 range over 48-52h
Source batches maintained DO2 >= ~7.4 mg/L throughout 96h — receiving-specific oxygen transfer failure
Product still rising: P=0.90 g/L @36h, 2.33 g/L @48h (delayed assays)
Forward model: strong_feed_reduction gives lowest oxygen deficit 3.79 mg-h/L, min DO 1.16 mg/L, highest product mass 131.8 kg; all other actions worse (deficit 6.5-8.2)
args.rationale: Receiving batch suffers an oxygen-transfer failure: DO2 collapsed from ~12 to ~3.3 mg/L at 46.2 h and is now fluctuating at/below the 2.0 mg/L minimum (1.67-2.3 mg/L at 48-52 h), unlike any source batch. Product is still accumulating (0.90 -> 2.33 g/L from 36 to 48 h), so oxygen demand remains high. Among bounded interventions, the source-calibrated forward model (imperfect, transfer multiplier ~0.44) ranks strong_feed_reduction best: lowest oxygen deficit (3.79 vs 6.5-8.2 mg-h/L), highest retained product mass (131.8 kg, since reduced feed lowers dilution volume), while cutting metabolic oxygen demand 40% and raising aeration 15%. Stop yields zero counted production; keep continues the violation. Recommend strong feed reduction with 15% air increase, with continued DO2 monitoring.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not receiving-truth; all its sensitivity members show post-decision DO2 remaining below 2.0 mg/L, so no bounded action is projected to fully clear the constraint. Strong_feed_reduction is the best bounded mitigation, not a guaranteed fix — actual receiving kinetics, oxygen demand, and transfer capacity are hidden. If DO2 remains below 2 mg/L after the change, escalation beyond the bounded menu would be warranted.
